newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Four cleared to run for Gambia presidency.
newsitem.headline: Four cleared to run for Gambia presidency.

text.p: Four candidates, among them coup leader Yahya Jammeh, have been cleared to contest Gambia's September 26 presidential election, the head of the independent election commission said on Saturday.

Gabriel Roberts told reporters that Jammeh, lawyer Ousainou Darboe of the United Democratic Party, Sidia Jatta of the small People's Democratic Organisation for Independence and Socialism, and hotel manager Amath Bah had fulfilled all the requirements and were eligible to stand.

He said breaches of the electoral code, including obstruction of the electoral commission or soldiers in uniform wearing badges or emblems of candidates, were punishable by law. "We want to ensure free and fair elections," he said.
Campaigning runs from September 9 to 24. Candidates are free to withdraw up until September 18.

Jammeh, who toppled elected civilian president Sir Dawda Jawara in a July 1994 coup accusing him of corruption, has resigned from the army to stand. Earlier, he barred anyone who served as a minister under Jawara from contesting elections.
The Commonwealth has described rules for the election and for parliamentary polls in December as flawed, saying they will allow the military to strengthen their grip on power.
The tiny country, surrounded by Senegal, traditionally depends on tourism, farming and aid to keep its economy afloat.
